verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?

verdicts.photo_observation: The route is documented as a sequence of annotated overlay photos rather than one continuous shot: a red 'DC Cable' line runs down the exterior wall to a labeled 'hole' (page 13); inside, the same red line continues from that hole through a 'UPS point' to the 'Inverter and its accessories' and 'Battery' boxes (page 14); a green 'AC Earthing Cable' line then runs from near the inverter room, through another labeled hole, down to a labeled 'AC Earth Pit' (pages 14-15); separately, an orange 'LA Cable' line runs from the rooftop tank area down the building exterior (page 17) toward a yellow 'LA PIT' marker (page 18); and an 'Equipment Location' photo (page 18) shows the Main Meter and Solar Meter positions connected by a line. Each segment's line color matches the Cable Routing Legend on page 4, and each line terminates at a labeled point (hole, pit, inverter, battery, meter) rather than ending in open space.
verdicts.rationale: Across the annotated photos, each cable-color segment (DC, AC earthing, LA) connects from a clear origin to a clear, labeled termination with no dangling/orphan line ends, and colors are used consistently with the legend; conduit/holes are explicitly called out at wall penetrations. The full run is documented as a chain of separate schematic overlays (typical for this report format) rather than a single unbroken photograph, which is the expected presentation style rather than a defect.
